text:
Alex M: heads up — eu-west2 gpu pool is seeing nvme lease thrash after the auto-drain yesterday, several launches stuck in provisioning.
ops-oncall: ALERT: node-pool-eu-west2-2 high io_wait > 75% (auto-alert).
Priya S: any logs? is this scrub/janitor hitting at the same time as batch windows?
Jamal R: pasting dmesg + iostat snapshot, looks like long svc times on nvme nodes:
```
  [ 1234.567890] nvme0: I/O 0xabcdef timeout after 30s, retrying
  [ 1234.600000] nvme0n1: write_map error -5
  iostat -x 1 3
Device            r/s    w/s  rkB/s  wkB/s avgrq-sz await svctm  %util
nvme0n1         0.50  120.00  32k   3800k   32.0   20.5   1.20   98.5
nvme1n1         0.10   60.00   8k   1900k   32.0   25.4   1.10   96.2
```
Jamal R: i see a pattern: janitor jobs started overlapping with aggressive batch launches after drain window. lease/metadata ops spike and slab locks pile up.
Kate H: can we pause the janitor/scrub on the impacted pool? what's the safe knob?
janitor-bot: scrub-schedule for eu-west2 nodes: next run 02:15 UTC, concurrency=12, target-rate=120MB/s.
Alex M: urgent mitigation: reduce janitor concurrency to 2 and throttle to 50MB/s, or pause for 30m. also lower batch parallelism for GPU provisioning (from 8 -> 2) while we triage.
Priya S: agreed. Jamal — can you run `echo 2 > /sys/fs/janitor/concurrency` and `systemctl stop nvme-scrub@eu-west2.service` on the two worst nodes? I'll patch the rollout policy to avoid that pool for 10m.
Jamal R: doing the stop now. posting ssh command used:
```
ssh node-123 'sudo systemctl stop nvme-scrub@eu-west2.service && sudo sh -c "echo 2 > /sys/fs/janitor/concurrency"'
```
Leo N: note: pausing scrub will increase wear backlog, but it's better than total provisioning failure. we should also add per-node iops cgroup for janitor to 20% so it can't saturate.
Kate H: can we add a quick admission control on the API side to block large parallel GPU starts into eu-west2 until health recovers?
Alex M: yes — will set route rule to steer new requests to eu-central and us-west as fallback. low-effort fix.
Priya S: monitoring: adding a temporary alert for nvme svc > 15ms and node provisioning queue > 3.
Jamal R: scrub stop applied to node-123/124/129. observed immediate drop in avgrq-sz and %util falling to ~35% in 45s.
ops-oncall: NOTE: incident escalated to infra-oncall. Cost note: 6 blocked GPU launches ~2h -> estimated lost revenue/opportunity ~ $420.
Alex M: next steps: (1) run a conservative scrub concurrency plan and rollout it (2) implement janitor iops cgroup (3) add scheduling affinity so scrub avoids heavy-provision windows (4) add a canary that detects lease thrash and auto-throttles janitor.
Priya S: I'll own the canary + alerting. Jamal, please open a small runbook with the commands we used.
Jamal R: creating runbook PR now, will include quick commands and the iostat/dmesg snippets.
Kate H: long term: consider metadata namespace sharding on disk and a less aggressive drain schedule for eu-west2 — storage team should weigh in.
Alex M: thanks everyone. if the scrub resume is safe, we can slowly ramp concurrency back over next 24h. ping here when nodes are fully back to normal. :thumbsup:
